Thanks for the redlines; received both files. I'll do an initial pass with Markus and loop in Marissa on the billing impacts. Quick answers up front:

- Seasonal carveout: potentially workable, we need to understand the historical monthly variance window you expect (60/90 days?) and whether this applies to committed vs. burst usage.
- Soft cap on overages: we have guardrail options but cap levels affect how we allocate burst capacity across customers; need an ops feasibility check.
- 30-day notice on model/quantization changes: reasonable to discuss, but we need to preserve the right to emergency patches; propose exception language for urgent security/compatibility fixes.

I'll come back with a redline that maps to Exhibit language (caps/floors table + billing mapping). Markus — can you confirm if the soft-cap ask triggers any invoice metric changes? Marissa — FYI for billing playbook.

Jeff / Kim —

Operational notes after a quick infra check:

- Soft cap (20% over published unit rate): technically implementable, but we need to define the measurement period and whether the cap applies per billing cycle or per invoice. Our preference is per invoice with cap applied at aggregate token-tier level to avoid per-request enforcement overhead.
- If BlueWillow expects the cap to be honored across model variants (e.g., if we route to a higher-cost model in a failover), we need contractual clarity and a fallback pricing matrix. Otherwise, we reserve the right to bill based on the actual serving variant.
- Seasonal carveout: recommend a 3-month rolling window with a defined baseline (avg of prior 12 months or 3-month trailing average). This will tie clearly into true-up calculations.

I've sketched suggested language and inserted comments in the attached Exhibit v2 (see docx). If these points look acceptable, we can prepare a narrow order-form amendment and present the compromise to legal.

Markus Klein
VP, Serving Reliability Operations
markus_klein@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 08:22:00 -07:00

Kimberly / Markus —

Thanks for the quick review. A few clarifying points from our side:

- BlueWillow prefers the cap to operate per invoice, applied at the aggregate token tier level — agree with Markus on the implementation rationale.
- For the model-variant issue, we would like a commitment that Redwood will not route us to materially higher-cost variants without notice and a cost pass-through agreement. If you must route for reliability, we ask for an automatic 10% credit on the incremental delta for that invoice period.
- Seasonal carveout: we can accept a 3-month rolling window but ask that the baseline be the 3-month trailing average (not 12 months) to avoid penalizing rapid growth.

Attached: BlueWillow-redlines-annotated.pdf (highlights on the variant/credit ask).

Please propose final exhibit text and we will route to our internal counsel for sign-off.

Best,
Anya Feldman
Sr. Contracts Counsel
BlueWillow Systems
